title: Best-of-N, majority voting, and weighted voting
goal:
The paper evaluates a reward model by best-of-$N$ search: sample $N$ solutions, keep the one the reward model ranks highest, and grade its final answer (Section 2.1). Majority voting is the baseline, and the paper also tried reward-model-weighted voting (Section 3). Write three functions:

- `best_of_n(scores)` returns the index of the highest score in a list of floats. The first index wins a tie.
- `majority_vote(answers)` returns the answer that occurs most often in a list of hashable answers. Among answers with the same count, the one that appears first in the list wins.
- `weighted_vote(answers, scores)` returns the answer whose scores add up to the largest total. Among answers with the same total, the one that appears first wins.

The tests use the five-candidate example from the page, where the ORM and majority voting pick the wrong answer and the PRM picks the right one.
hints: For `best_of_n`, keep the index of the best score so far and replace it only when a score is strictly greater. That rule keeps the first index on a tie.
`collections.Counter(answers).most_common(1)` returns the first-seen answer among tied counts, because `Counter` keeps insertion order.
For `weighted_vote`, add each score to a dictionary entry for its answer. A dictionary keeps insertion order, so scan it in order and replace the best only on a strictly larger total.
Do not use `max(answers)`. Answers are labels and have no order that matters here.
